The long hand ticks its way past the finish line and I exhale sharply. Why do I keep betting on the short one? It never wins.

Rows of buzzing fluorescent lights flicker above ratty carpeted cubicle walls. They smell like a dumpster. Bob only spends money on his convertible and breast implants, not his company.

Marie giggles and slides my last quarter next to her small pile “I win! Too bad you’re out of money. We could have played again.”

I blink sweat from my eyes. Bob wouldn’t spend money on air conditioning either. “I don’t have it in my convertible anyway” he’d say.

Marie is staring at me, her head sideways. “We could do something else…” her voice trails off and sweat glistens on her throat. She slides a pill toward me. “It’s called molly. It’s fun, even more fun than betting on clocks”

I shake my head “Bob will find out”

“Bob won’t find out”

“Bob always finds out”

“Bob always finds out what?” Bob asks walking into the office. I should have heard his cargo shorts. Marie and I look at each other “That the short hand never wins” I say. “That it’s oppressively hot in here” Marie talks over me.

Bob doesn't say anything. His angry eye twitches. “Ryan, the letter from insurance. Do you have it? I told you to find it by noon.”

“It’s only 10”

“I don’t care.” His voice turns up at the end like it’s a question. He does a thing with his hand at the same time. Fuck you, Bob.

I hand him the letter. There’s a garbage stain along the edge of the envelope. It had been resting against the cubicle, after all.

Bob takes the letter and leaves, his silk Hawaiian shirt rippling behind him. “Motherfuckers said they aren’t gonna pay for Dolly’s tits” I hear him mutter.

I look at the pill. It’s still on the desk, this whole time. Bob didn't say anything. I look at Marie and she raises her eyebrows.

“Bob always finds out” Bob shouts from down the hall.

“Look,” Marie whispers “I have another one. I have a lot of them. I’ll do it if you will.” She holds a pill between her teeth. I pick up the other one and bring it to my face. Marie flips the bird toward the door. I laugh and swallow the pill. Marie flashes a grin.

Today is Tuesday. I have just as many quarters in my pile as when I started. Marie and I keep betting on the same hand.

“This isn't as exciting as when I bet on the slow one” I say.

“The slow one never wins, you know that” Marie blinks with every tick and tock. It’s annoying. “We could do what we did the other day” she muses.

“But Bob…” I start

“But Bob nothing. He didn't find out. Have you seen him since yesterday anyway?”

“No, but”

“No buts! He’s probably in Pensacola driving his new stripper girlfriend around”

“If it makes you stop blinking like that, fine”

Marie stands from her seat on the desk and pulls two pills from the pocket of her frayed jean shorts. I reach for one and feel my shirt sticking to my back. “Christ it’s hot in here”.

“On three” Marie says. “One, Three!” she shouts and tosses the pill in the air. I swallow mine before she catches hers in her mouth.

“I need to use the…” Marie says as she tilts her head toward the restroom. I nod and shift in my seat. God, even my socks are stuck to my skin. I stare at the clock and wait for Marie. It’s so white, nailed to yellow walls. Whoever rented this building for the past hundred years must have smoked a carton a day.

I count the seconds. Then the minutes. Then the hours. Then I saw it – the hour hand moved faster than the others. For a full circle, then another and another. I couldn't believe it. I knew it was possible. It stopped at 6 o’clock. Time to go home.

I looked around for Marie. She must have left already. I grab my briefcase and jacket and take a step toward the hallway. “This is Bob’s hallway. Bob’s hallway to heaven. Use the peasants’ door.” I hear Bob in my head.

I sigh and turn around. The front door is so far from the parking lot, I don’t know why we can’t use this one, too.

Today is Wednesday. Marie is cackling like a maniac, dragging her fingers over her pile of quarters. The shitty lights flicker on the edges and I just feel angry. I saw the short hand win, I know I did.

“You’re out of luck and out of money, honey” Marie gloats “Doesn’t it always end like this? It’s not a secret, but that’s how I can afford these” She slides a pill toward me.

I don’t wait for her to take hers. I just swallow it glumly.

“I need to take out the trash” she says. I blink in acquiescence.

It’s six o’clock and Marie still hasn't returned. She must have left early. I grab my briefcase and notice Marie didn't swallow her pill, it’s still on the desk. She won’t miss it. “The short hand fucking wins” I think while I swallow.

Today is Thursday. I haven’t seen Marie all day. Or Bob for that matter. I haven’t seen Bob all week. What an asshole. “Ryan do this, Ryan do that”. I don’t even know what Marie does except take out the trash. I do everything.

It’s lunchtime and I've been watching the clock all day. The short hand never wins.

“Hello? Excuse me?” a raspy voice calls. A wrinkled woman wearing a white skirt and a white apron stands in the doorway.

“Hi, can I help you?”

“My name is Marie, and I've been asked to give you these.” The woman pulls a small bottle from her pocket. “A friend said you might want them”. She tries to wink but it looks like she’s having a stroke.

“What are they? What friend?”

“Oh there now,” she coos “I’ll take one if you do”. She tries to wink again and holds a pill between her teeth.

Whatever. I swallow it with my eyes closed. When I open them the woman is gone and it’s six o’clock.

I turn to see Old Marie standing in her starchy white apron.
